title: Mastery needs breadth across item families
statement: Base a mastery decision on several different items from several item families, because passing by retrying near-identical items, or on a handful of items, is practice, not mastery.
example: One review treats a gate decision on fewer than 10 items as retrieval practice, not mastery.
detail: The red-team taxonomy's "grind-through gate" is passed by retrying near-identical items; its rule is that mastery evidence must span item families, and that a gate decision on fewer than 10 items is retrieval practice, not mastery (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/course-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`). The grade 3 item criteria ask for breadth across item families and near-miss contrasts, with recovery verified, and never rest a mastery decision on a single multiple-choice item, with its guess rate of 25% or more (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/dimensions/D5-assessment-item-construction.md`).
